acceptance: The effective default for --capture-plans is reconciled against prior recorded decisions and documented consistently in CLI help, Python API docs and feature docs; any change that adds execution cost is an explicit design decision.
An executable CLI check distinguishes omitted analyze flag, explicit --analyze-plans and --no-analyze-plans using actual per-operator timing presence; all three agree with the published contract.
Documentation distinguishes capture opt-in, deferred-phase eligibility and actual adapter/parser capability; it distinguishes normalized logical fingerprints from full physical-plan equivalence.

Documentation accurately describes SQL versus DataFrame result fields and the limits of post-measurement EXPLAIN, including bespoke mid-run mutations; remove the unsupported DuckDB estimate-leak exception.
context: Observed 2026-10-28: TPC-H DuckDB Q1/Q6 capture succeeded both with --no-analyze-plans and with no analyze flag. The default bundle had timing=null and cardinality=null on physical operators, matching the false adapter default rather than CLI help. Existing phase tests exercise explicit true/false, not the documented CLI default. Intended logical-hash and post-measurement limitations are not requests to redesign capture.
description: CLI help and query-plan-analysis.md promise ANALYZE capture by default, but PlatformAdapter defaults analyze_plans to false and a real CLI run without either analyze flag captured estimated plans with null operator timing. Other contract drift includes treating phase eligibility as support, a documented DuckDB estimate-fingerprint exception not supported by the structural signature, and generic result-field claims that do not hold for raw DataFrame wrappers. Reconcile prior decisions before choosing the default: completed qpc-04 explicitly chose estimated plans, while later completed items/documentation describe ANALYZE defaults. Do not silently enable query re-execution merely to match prose.
